newsitem.title: USA: Latin American Casinos sees EPS rising.
newsitem.headline: Latin American Casinos sees EPS rising.

text.p: Latin American Casinos Inc said Wednesday it expects earnings per share to increase in each successive quarter of 1997.
Latin American Casinos reported first quarter earnings of $0.02 a share on revenues of $426,000, compared to $0.10 a share on revenues of $587,000 a year earlier.
The company said first quarter revenue was nine percent higher than revenue in the 1996 fourth quarter, when the company lost $0.03 a share.
Latin American Casinos said it sees revenue and profit increases from expansion of its new gaming route operations in Colombia, Nicaragua and Honduras.
"Under gaming route operations, the company recoups 70 percent of the profits generated by each slot machine," Lloyd Lyons, chief executive officer, said in a press release.

"We expect this change to increase revenues and cash flow and to reduce allowances for doubtful accounts. Latin American Casinos Inc is now squarely in the gaming route business and is no longer strictly a rental company," he said.

The company said it is financially strong with over $9.6 million in assets, consisting of $4.3 million in cash and cash equivalents, 7,000 slot machines in inventory, no debt, and a tax loss carry-forward of $874,000.
In addition, the company has available foreign tax credits of $275,000.
